messages:
Maya: wrapping up night shift in ~10m. quick heads-up — we just saw a KV-cache eviction storm in us-west-2 hitting inference nodes. routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream showing p95 latency jumps. I'm handing off now — anyone primary, please confirm and take over.

Ken: ack. rough numbers?

Maya: p50 gen from ~120ms to ~350ms, p95 from ~450ms to ~1.2s. error-rate for streams up ~0.3% (idle client disconnects). traffic spike seemed cache-localized — prefix/KV hit rate dropped from 87% -> 42% in 3m.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 | severity: P2 | affected: inference-us-west-2 | pager targets: @sre-oncall-primary -> 5m -> @sre-lead -> @infra-lead. Runbook: https://playbook.internal/redwood/kv-cache-eviction

Oliver: I can take primary for the handoff. jumping in now. first action: validate cache metrics + tail logs for OOM/eviction events.

Maya: checklist I'm leaving in thread:
- confirm primary/secondary (done)
- note customer impact (internal summary below)
- mitigation attempt: warm-restart small shard group, ramp down cache warming traffic
- if no improvement in 10m escalate per pager policy

Maya: customer impact (short): intermittent higher latency for generation endpoints in US-W. No broad 5xx spike, some stream disconnects affecting long-stream sessions. Potentially impacts high-throughput customers and low-latency webhooks.

Ken: copy. if we need to escalate earlier? what's our threshold here for immediate escalation to leads?

Oliver: my proposal: if p95 > 1s sustained for 5m OR error-rate >0.5% then escalate to @sre-lead immediately. otherwise attempt two warm restarts (one small shard, then group) + rehydrate cache. if after restart p95 still >800ms for 5m, escalate.

Maya: agree. also note ticketing: mark incident P2 and link to customer-facing impact doc when we know affected tenants.

sre-oncall-primary: starting with targeted warm restart of shard-7 (non-disruptive attempt):

```bash
# targeted warm restart (examples, run in infra cluster namespace)
kubectl -n inference rollout restart sts/kv-cache-shard-7 --grace-period=60
# monitor cache hit metric: telemetry.query('kv_cache_hit_rate{shard="7"}')
```

sre-oncall-primary: also lowering max-prefix-warmth to reduce churn: set config key kv.prefix_warm_threshold=0.6 for target shards. rolling change in 3 steps.

incident-bot: Pager issued to @sre-oncall-primary at 1739001300. Escalation timer: 300s.

Ken: tagging runbook snippet for quick reference: https://playbook.internal/redwood/kv-cache-eviction#warm-restart and runbook has escalation matrix (page -> after 5m -> leads -> call).

Oliver: restart kicked at 1739001356. monitoring. current metrics: p95 down to 780ms, p50 220ms, stream errors stable.

Maya: nice. reminder on paging rules for this kind of degraded-latency P2:
- page primary first (default), wait 5m.
- if no ack or no mitigation, escalate to SRE Lead + Infra Lead.
- for multi-region customer-impacting events, escalate immediately to Eng PM + CSM.
- if any data-loss risk -> immediate bridge + executive notify.

sre-oncall-primary: update after second step: warming rehydration running, p95 now ~560ms. looks like rehydrate helped.

Ken: if things improve, what handoff notes should be left for next shift?

Oliver: leave: timeline of events, commands run, which shards restarted, metrics before/after, link to logs (elk://search/INC-2026-0421), and open follow-up to investigate root cause (possible cache eviction thrash under uneven hot keys). Also add an action item: add autoscale rule to increase cache replicas when fill-rate >80% for 1m.

Maya: also note coverage gap: my primary shift ends in 9m, and the next shift coverage window overlaps but secondary is on PTO tomorrow. Oliver, confirm you can cover until secondary is backfilled or we reassign.

Oliver: I can cover the next 2h. will create a quick note in rotation and ping ops to patch secondary.

incident-bot: Pager timer cleared at 1739003000 (ack received). Incident status: mitigating.

sre-oncall-primary: leaving final note before warmhandoff: mitigations applied, p95 stabilized under 600ms, tracking follow-ups, handing to Maya's replacement or Ken if they take next shift. next-check in 30m or sooner if any regression. :thumbsup:

Maya: thanks all — leaving thread. if anything regresses, please page per policy and reference INC-2026-0421. :phone: 

Ken: thanks — adding follow-up action items and assigning to infra-team for root-cause. :memo:

Oliver: closing handoff — I've added the runbook edits for clearer autoscale steps. logging final metrics snapshot in the incident ticket.

Maya: confirmed. off now. good job.
